AI.title_translation: Bench-NPIN：非抓取式交互导航的基准测试
AI.tldr: 提出了Bench-NPIN，这是首个针对非抓取式交互导航（如推动物体）的综合基准测试，它提供了一系列模拟环境、专门的评估指标，并用于评估现有基线，以提高该领域研究的复现性和可比性。
AI.motivation: 移动机器人在非结构化环境中需要进行交互式导航（与可移动物体进行战略性互动）。现有的非抓取式交互导航（NPIN）解决方案通常使用特定案例的设置进行评估，这限制了研究的复现性和跨系统比较。
AI.method: 提出了Bench-NPIN，这是第一个综合性的非抓取式交互导航基准测试，它是一个开源Python库，具有模块化设计。该基准包含三个主要组件：1) 一系列用于非抓取式交互导航任务的综合模拟环境（如带可移动障碍的迷宫、冰水中的自主船舶导航、箱子递送和区域清理）；2) 一套捕捉交互式导航独特方面的评估指标（如效率、交互努力和部分任务完成度）；3) 用于评估现有基线在不同环境中的示例实现的演示。
AI.result: 演示了使用Bench-NPIN来评估现有基线在不同环境中的实现。
AI.translation: 移动机器人的部署越来越多地出现在障碍物和物体均可移动的非结构化环境中。在这种环境中的导航被称为交互式导航，任务完成不仅需要避开障碍物，还需要与可移动物体进行战略性互动。非抓取式交互导航侧重于非抓取式的交互策略，例如推，而不是依赖抓取式操作。尽管该领域的研究日益增多，但大多数解决方案都是使用特定案例的设置进行评估，这限制了复现性和交叉比较。在本文中，我们提出了Bench-NPIN，这是第一个针对非抓取式交互导航的综合基准测试。Bench-NPIN包含多个组件：1）一系列用于非抓取式交互导航任务的综合模拟环境，包括穿越带有可移动障碍物的迷宫、冰水中的自主船舶导航、箱子递送和区域清理，每个环境具有不同的复杂程度；2）一套捕捉交互式导航独特方面的评估指标，例如效率、交互努力和部分任务完成度；3）使用Bench-NPIN来评估现有基线在不同环境中的示例实现的演示。Bench-NPIN是一个具有模块化设计的开源Python库。代码、文档和训练模型可在https://github.com/IvanIZ/BenchNPIN找到。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了Bench-NPIN，这是首个针对非抓取式交互导航（NPIN）的综合基准测试平台。NPIN是移动机器人在包含可移动障碍的非结构化环境中通过推等非抓取方式进行策略性交互的导航方式。鉴于现有研究缺乏统一的评估标准，Bench-NPIN旨在提高该领域研究的复现性和可比性。该基准包含多样的模拟环境（如迷宫、冰上航行、递送任务），一套专门的评估指标（包括效率和交互努力），以及用于评估现有基线实现的工具。Bench-NPIN作为一个开源Python库发布。
AI.keywords: 非抓取式交互, 交互式导航, 基准测试, 移动机器人, 模拟
AI.comments: Bench-NPIN的创新性在于它解决了移动机器人交互式导航领域长期存在的评估标准化问题。通过提供统一的模拟环境、多样的任务和专门的指标（如交互努力和部分任务完成度），它极大地促进了非抓取式交互导航算法的公平比较和快速迭代。其重要性在于，非抓取式交互（如推动）在许多现实世界的机器人应用中比抓取更实用或更高效，建立一个强大的、开源的基准对于推动该子领域的发展至关重要。

title: HBO: Hierarchical Balancing Optimization for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on a mixture of diverse datasets poses challenges due to data imbalance and heterogeneity. Existing methods often address these issues across datasets (globally) but overlook the imbalance and heterogeneity within individual datasets (locally), which limits their effectiveness. We introduce Hierarchical Balancing Optimization (HBO), a novel method that enables LLMs to autonomously adjust data allocation during fine-tuning both across datasets (globally) and within each individual dataset (locally). HBO employs a bilevel optimization strategy with two types of actors: a Global Actor, which balances data sampling across different subsets of the training mixture, and several Local Actors, which optimizes data usage within each subset based on difficulty levels. These actors are guided by reward functions derived from the LLM's training state, which measure learning progress and relative performance improvement. We evaluate HBO on three LLM backbones across nine diverse tasks in multilingual and multitask setups. Results show that HBO consistently outperforms existing baselines, achieving significant accuracy gains. Our in-depth analysis further demonstrates that both the global actor and local actors of HBO effectively adjust data usage during fine-tuning. HBO provides a comprehensive solution to the challenges of data imbalance and heterogeneity in LLM fine-tuning, enabling more effective training across diverse datasets.

AI.title_translation: HBO：用于微调大型语言模型的层次化平衡优化
AI.tldr: 针对LLM微调中数据不平衡和异构性问题，提出HBO（层次化平衡优化），它使用全局和局部双层优化策略，根据学习进度自动调整数据分配，显著提升了多任务和多语言设置下的模型性能。
AI.motivation: 在混合多样数据集上微调大型语言模型（LLMs）时，面临数据不平衡和异构性的挑战。现有方法主要解决数据集间的全局不平衡，而忽略了单个数据集内部的局部不平衡和异构性，限制了微调效果。
AI.method: 提出层次化平衡优化（HBO），采用双层优化策略，使LLMs能自主调整全局（跨数据集）和局部（数据集内）的数据分配。它包含一个全局Actor（平衡跨子集采样）和多个局部Actor（基于难度优化数据集内使用），这些Actor由衡量学习进度和相对性能提升的奖励函数指导。
AI.result: 在三种LLM骨干模型和九个多语言、多任务设置的测试中，HBO始终优于现有基线，实现了显著的准确性提升。深入分析表明，全局和局部Actor都能有效调整微调过程中的数据使用。
AI.conclusion: HBO为LLM微调中数据不平衡和异构性的挑战提供了一个全面的解决方案，从而能够在多样化数据集上实现更有效的训练。
AI.translation: 在多样化数据集混合体上微调大型语言模型（LLMs）由于数据不平衡和异构性而面临挑战。现有方法通常在跨数据集（全局）层面解决这些问题，但忽略了单个数据集内部（局部）的不平衡和异构性，这限制了它们的有效性。我们引入了层次化平衡优化（HBO），这是一种新颖的方法，使LLMs能够在微调过程中自主调整跨数据集（全局）和每个单独数据集内部（局部）的数据分配。HBO采用双层优化策略，包含两种类型的Actor：一个全局Actor，用于平衡训练混合体不同子集之间的数据采样；以及几个局部Actor，用于根据难度级别优化每个子集内的数据使用。这些Actor由源自LLM训练状态的奖励函数指导，这些奖励函数衡量学习进度和相对性能改进。我们在多语言和多任务设置中，使用三种LLM骨干模型对九项不同任务进行了HBO的评估。结果显示，HBO持续优于现有基线，实现了显著的准确性提升。我们深入的分析进一步证明，HBO的全局Actor和局部Actor都能在微调过程中有效调整数据使用。HBO为LLM微调中数据不平衡和异构性的挑战提供了一个全面的解决方案，从而能够在多样化数据集上实现更有效的训练。
AI.summary: 本文提出了HBO（层次化平衡优化），旨在解决LLM在混合数据集上微调时面临的全局和局部数据不平衡及异构性问题。HBO采用双层优化策略，通过全局Actor平衡跨数据集采样，并通过局部Actor基于难度优化数据集内使用。这些Actor由衡量学习进度的奖励函数驱动，实现了数据的自主调整分配。实验证明，在多任务和多语言设置中，HBO显著优于现有基线，能更有效地利用多样化数据集进行训练。
AI.keywords: 层次化平衡优化, 大型语言模型微调, 数据不平衡, 双层优化, 数据异构性
AI.comments: 本文的创新点在于提出了层次化（全局和局部）数据平衡优化策略，解决了现有方法仅关注全局不平衡的局限性。通过引入基于学习进度奖励函数的双层优化Actor机制，实现了数据分配的自主调整，这在LLM微调的数据采样领域具有重要的创新意义。该方法对于提高LLM在复杂、多样化、非均衡混合数据集上的训练效率和泛化能力具有重要的实际价值。

title: Physics-Driven Local-Whole Elastic Deformation Modeling for Point Cloud Representation Learning
summary: Existing point cloud representation learning methods primarily rely on data-driven strategies to extract geometric information from large amounts of scattered data. However, most methods focus solely on the spatial distribution features of point clouds while overlooking the relationship between local information and the whole structure, which limits the accuracy of point cloud representation. Local information reflect the fine-grained variations of an object, while the whole structure is determined by the interaction and combination of these local features, collectively defining the object's shape. In real-world, objects undergo deformation under external forces, and this deformation gradually affects the whole structure through the propagation of forces from local regions, thereby altering the object's geometric features. Therefore, appropriately introducing a physics-driven mechanism to capture the topological relationships between local parts and the whole object can effectively mitigate for the limitations of data-driven point cloud methods in structural modeling, and enhance the generalization and interpretability of point cloud representations for downstream tasks such as understanding and recognition. Inspired by this, we incorporate a physics-driven mechanism into the data-driven method to learn fine-grained features in point clouds and model the structural relationship between local regions and the whole shape. Specifically, we design a dual-task encoder-decoder framework that combines the geometric modeling capability of data-driven implicit fields with physics-driven elastic deformation. Through the integration of physics-based loss functions, the framework is guided to predict localized deformation and explicitly capture the correspondence between local structural changes and whole shape variations.

AI.title_translation: 物理驱动的局部-整体弹性形变建模用于点云表示学习
AI.tldr: 针对传统点云学习方法忽略局部与整体结构关系的问题，本文提出了一种结合数据驱动隐式场和物理驱动弹性形变的双任务编解码框架。通过引入基于物理的损失函数，该方法能捕获局部形变与整体形状变化的对应关系，从而提高点云表示的准确性、泛化性和可解释性。
AI.motivation: 现有数据驱动的点云表示学习方法只关注点云的空间分布特征，忽略了局部信息与整体结构之间的关系，限制了点云表示的准确性。现实世界中物体形变是局部力向整体结构传播的结果。因此，引入物理驱动机制来捕获局部部件与整体物体之间的拓扑关系，可以弥补数据驱动方法的局限性，增强泛化性和可解释性。
AI.method: 设计了一个双任务（dual-task）编码器-解码器框架。该框架将数据驱动的隐式场的几何建模能力与物理驱动的弹性形变相结合。通过集成基于物理的损失函数，该框架被引导来预测局部形变，并显式地捕获局部结构变化与整体形状变化之间的对应关系。
AI.translation: 现有的点云表示学习方法主要依赖数据驱动策略从大量的分散数据中提取几何信息。然而，大多数方法只关注点云的空间分布特征，而忽略了局部信息与整体结构之间的关系，这限制了点云表示的准确性。局部信息反映了物体的细粒度变化，而整体结构则由这些局部特征的相互作用和组合决定，共同定义了物体的形状。在现实世界中，物体在外部力的作用下会发生形变，这种形变通过力从局部区域的传播逐渐影响整体结构，从而改变物体的几何特征。因此，适当引入物理驱动机制来捕获局部部件与整体物体之间的拓扑关系，可以有效地减轻数据驱动点云方法在结构建模上的局限性，并增强点云表示在理解和识别等下游任务中的泛化性和可解释性。受此启发，我们将物理驱动机制融入数据驱动方法中，以学习点云中的细粒度特征，并建模局部区域与整体形状之间的结构关系。具体来说，我们设计了一个双任务编码器-解码器框架，将数据驱动隐式场的几何建模能力与物理驱动的弹性形变相结合。通过集成基于物理的损失函数，该框架被引导来预测局部形变，并显式地捕获局部结构变化与整体形状变化之间的对应关系。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种物理驱动的局部-整体弹性形变建模方法，用于点云表示学习。针对传统数据驱动方法忽略局部与整体结构关联的缺陷，研究人员将物理驱动机制（基于弹性形变）融入到数据驱动方法中。具体实现是一个双任务编码器-解码器框架，它结合了隐式场的几何建模能力和物理驱动的损失函数，旨在预测局部形变并显式捕捉局部结构变化如何影响整体形状，从而提升点云表示的结构建模能力、泛化性和可解释性。
AI.keywords: 点云表示学习, 物理驱动, 弹性形变, 局部-整体结构, 双任务框架
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于将物理学原理（弹性形变）引入到传统的数据驱动点云学习框架中。这种“物理驱动”与“数据驱动”的结合，旨在解决现有方法在结构建模中缺乏局部-整体拓扑关系的问题。通过模拟现实世界中物体在受力下的形变过程，该方法有望显著提高点云表示的准确性、泛化性和可解释性，尤其是在处理需要细粒度结构理解的下游任务时。这种跨学科的融合为点云表示学习提供了一个新的、更具解释性的方向。

title: LEANCODE: Understanding Models Better for Code Simplification of Pre-trained Large Language Models
comments: ACL 2025 Main. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/akai-sh/LeanCode
summary: Large Language Models for code often entail significant computational complexity, which grows significantly with the length of the input code sequence. We propose LeanCode for code simplification to reduce training and prediction time, leveraging code contexts in utilizing attention scores to represent the tokens' importance. We advocate for the selective removal of tokens based on the average context-aware attention scores rather than average scores across all inputs. LeanCode uses the attention scores of `CLS' tokens within the encoder for classification tasks, such as code search. It also employs the encoder-decoder attention scores to determine token significance for sequence-to-sequence tasks like code summarization. Our evaluation shows LeanCode's superiority over the SOTAs DietCode and Slimcode, with improvements of 60% and 16% for code search, and 29% and 27% for code summarization, respectively.
comment: ACL 2025 Main. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/akai-sh/LeanCode

AI.title_translation: LEANCODE：更好地理解模型以简化预训练大型语言模型的代码
AI.tldr: LeanCode通过利用注意力分数选择性地删除不重要的token，从而简化代码，以减少代码大型语言模型的计算复杂性，并在代码搜索和代码摘要任务上优于现有技术。
AI.motivation: 大型语言模型处理代码时通常涉及显著的计算复杂性，且随着输入代码序列长度的增加而显著增长，因此需要一种代码简化方法来减少训练和预测时间。
AI.method: LeanCode利用代码上下文中的注意力分数来表示token的重要性，并基于平均上下文感知注意力分数选择性地删除token。对于代码搜索等分类任务，它使用编码器中`CLS` token的注意力分数；对于代码摘要等序列到序列任务，它使用编码器-解码器注意力分数来确定token的重要性。
AI.result: LeanCode在代码搜索方面比DietCode和Slimcode分别提高了60%和16%，在代码摘要方面分别提高了29%和27%。
AI.conclusion: LeanCode在代码搜索和代码摘要任务上表现优于现有技术DietCode和Slimcode。
AI.translation: 用于代码的大型语言模型通常涉及显著的计算复杂性，且随着输入代码序列长度的增加而显著增长。我们提出了LeanCode用于代码简化，以减少训练和预测时间，它利用代码上下文中的注意力分数来表示token的重要性。我们主张基于平均上下文感知注意力分数而不是所有输入上的平均分数来选择性地删除token。LeanCode在分类任务（如代码搜索）中使用编码器内`CLS` token的注意力分数。它还采用编码器-解码器注意力分数来确定序列到序列任务（如代码摘要）中token的重要性。我们的评估表明，LeanCode优于现有技术DietCode和Slimcode，在代码搜索方面分别提高了60%和16%，在代码摘要方面分别提高了29%和27%。
AI.summary: 本文提出了LeanCode，一种用于简化预训练大型语言模型代码的方法，旨在解决代码LLM高计算复杂性的问题。LeanCode通过利用上下文感知的注意力分数来识别并选择性地删除不重要的token，以减少训练和预测时间。它针对不同任务（如代码搜索和代码摘要）采用不同的注意力机制。实验结果表明，LeanCode在这些任务上的性能显著优于现有SOTA方法。
AI.keywords: 代码简化, 大型语言模型, 注意力分数, 计算复杂性, LeanCode
AI.comments: LeanCode的创新之处在于其利用上下文感知注意力分数进行选择性token删除的策略，这比简单地基于平均分数更精细。它针对不同类型的任务（分类与序列到序列）使用不同的注意力分数机制，显示了其方法的灵活性和任务适应性。该方法对于优化代码LLM的效率具有重要意义，尤其是在处理长代码序列时。

title: Image-to-Image Translation with Diffusion Transformers and CLIP-Based Image Conditioning
comments: Published in: 2025 6th International Conference on Computer Vision, Image and Deep Learning (CVIDL)
summary: Image-to-image translation aims to learn a mapping between a source and a target domain, enabling tasks such as style transfer, appearance transformation, and domain adaptation. In this work, we explore a diffusion-based framework for image-to-image translation by adapting Diffusion Transformers (DiT), which combine the denoising capabilities of diffusion models with the global modeling power of transformers. To guide the translation process, we condition the model on image embeddings extracted from a pre-trained CLIP encoder, allowing for fine-grained and structurally consistent translations without relying on text or class labels. We incorporate both a CLIP similarity loss to enforce semantic consistency and an LPIPS perceptual loss to enhance visual fidelity during training. We validate our approach on two benchmark datasets: face2comics, which translates real human faces to comic-style illustrations, and edges2shoes, which translates edge maps to realistic shoe images. Experimental results demonstrate that DiT, combined with CLIP-based conditioning and perceptual similarity objectives, achieves high-quality, semantically faithful translations, offering a promising alternative to GAN-based models for paired image-to-image translation tasks.

AI.title_translation: 使用扩散Transformer和基于CLIP的图像条件控制的图像到图像翻译
AI.tldr: 使用结合了扩散Transformer（DiT）和CLIP图像嵌入条件的框架进行图像到图像翻译，实现了高质量、语义准确的转换，优于传统方法。
AI.motivation: 图像到图像翻译旨在学习源域和目标域之间的映射，以实现风格迁移、外观转换和域适应等任务。作者希望探索一种新的、基于扩散的模型框架来实现这一目标。
AI.method: 探索了一个基于扩散的框架，通过适配扩散Transformer（DiT）来实现图像到图像的翻译。模型通过从预训练的CLIP编码器中提取的图像嵌入进行条件化，并结合了CLIP相似性损失和LPIPS感知损失进行训练。
AI.result: 在face2comics和edges2shoes两个基准数据集上验证了该方法，结果显示DiT结合CLIP条件控制和感知损失实现了高质量、语义忠实的翻译。
AI.conclusion: 实验结果表明，结合CLIP条件控制和感知相似性目标，DiT能够实现高质量、语义忠实的翻译，为成对图像到图像翻译任务提供了一种有前景的替代GAN的方法。
AI.translation: 图像到图像翻译旨在学习源域到目标域的映射，从而实现风格迁移、外观转换和域适应等任务。在这项工作中，我们探索了一种基于扩散的框架来进行图像到图像翻译，通过适配结合了扩散模型去噪能力和Transformer全局建模能力的扩散Transformer（DiT）。为了指导翻译过程，我们使用从预训练的CLIP编码器中提取的图像嵌入对模型进行条件化，从而实现在不依赖文本或类别标签的情况下进行精细和结构一致的翻译。我们在训练中结合了CLIP相似性损失以强制执行语义一致性，以及LPIPS感知损失以增强视觉保真度。我们在两个基准数据集上验证了我们的方法：face2comics，它将真实人脸转换为漫画风格的插图；以及edges2shoes，它将边缘图转换为逼真的鞋子图像。实验结果表明，DiT结合基于CLIP的条件控制和感知相似性目标，实现了高质量、语义忠实的翻译，为成对的图像到图像翻译任务提供了一种有前景的替代GAN模型的方法。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种新的基于扩散Transformer（DiT）的图像到图像翻译框架，该框架使用预训练CLIP编码器提取的图像嵌入作为条件，以实现无需文本标签的精细化、结构一致的翻译。通过引入CLIP相似性损失和LPIPS感知损失来保证语义一致性和视觉保真度，实验证明了该方法在标准数据集上取得了高质量的结果，是GAN模型的有力替代方案。
AI.keywords: 图像到图像翻译, 扩散Transformer, CLIP, 图像条件控制, 感知损失
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于将扩散Transformer（DiT）应用于图像到图像的翻译任务，并使用基于CLIP的图像嵌入进行条件控制，这提供了一种无需文本标签即可实现精细和结构一致翻译的新范式。其重要性在于为图像到图像翻译提供了一种有前景的、基于扩散模型的替代方案，可以与GAN模型竞争。局限性可能在于对预训练CLIP模型的依赖以及训练的计算成本。

title: SPhyR: Spatial-Physical Reasoning Benchmark on Material Distribution
summary: We introduce a novel dataset designed to benchmark the physical and spatial reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLM) based on topology optimization, a method for computing optimal material distributions within a design space under prescribed loads and supports. In this dataset, LLMs are provided with conditions such as 2D boundary, applied forces and supports, and must reason about the resulting optimal material distribution. The dataset includes a variety of tasks, ranging from filling in masked regions within partial structures to predicting complete material distributions. Solving these tasks requires understanding the flow of forces and the required material distribution under given constraints, without access to simulation tools or explicit physical models, challenging models to reason about structural stability and spatial organization. Our dataset targets the evaluation of spatial and physical reasoning abilities in 2D settings, offering a complementary perspective to traditional language and logic benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: SPhyR：材料分布的空间物理推理基准
AI.tldr: 该研究引入了一个新的数据集，用于评估大型语言模型在拓扑优化方面的空间和物理推理能力，模型需要根据给定的边界条件、力和支撑来预测最优材料分布，而不能使用模拟工具。
AI.motivation: 评估大型语言模型在拓扑优化方面的空间和物理推理能力。
AI.method: 创建一个包含2D边界、载荷和支撑条件的数据集，要求大型语言模型预测最优材料分布，包括填充掩码区域和预测完整分布。
AI.result: 该数据集包含多种任务，用于评估模型理解力、结构稳定性和空间组织能力，并为2D设置下的空间和物理推理提供了一个新的视角。
AI.conclusion: 该数据集为评估大型语言模型在物理和空间推理方面的能力提供了一个新的基准，特别是在拓扑优化领域。
AI.translation: 我们引入了一个新的数据集，旨在根据拓扑优化（一种在规定载荷和支撑下计算设计空间内最优材料分布的方法）来评估大型语言模型（LLM）的物理和空间推理能力。在此数据集中，LLM会获得诸如2D边界、施加的力和支撑等条件，并且必须推理由此产生的最优材料分布。该数据集包括各种任务，从填充部分结构中的掩码区域到预测完整的材料分布。解决这些任务需要理解力的流动以及给定约束下的所需材料分布，而无需访问仿真工具或显式物理模型，这对模型提出了推理结构稳定性和空间组织能力的要求。我们的数据集旨在评估2D设置下的空间和物理推理能力，为传统的语言和逻辑基准提供了补充视角。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了SPhyR数据集，用于评估大型语言模型在拓扑优化中的空间和物理推理能力。该数据集包含2D边界、载荷和支撑条件，模型需预测最优材料分布，挑战其在无仿真工具下的结构稳定性和空间组织推理能力。
AI.keywords: 拓扑优化, 空间推理, 物理推理, 大型语言模型, 数据集
AI.comments: 该研究通过引入一个基于拓扑优化的新数据集，为评估大型语言模型在物理和空间推理方面的能力提供了一个创新的方法。数据集的重点在于模型在没有显式物理模型或模拟工具的情况下进行推理的能力，这对于开发更通用的AI系统至关重要。然而，该数据集仅限于2D设置，未来的工作可以扩展到3D，并探索更复杂的物理现象。

title: Guided Diffusion Sampling on Function Spaces with Applications to PDEs
summary: We propose a general framework for conditional sampling in PDE-based inverse problems, targeting the recovery of whole solutions from extremely sparse or noisy measurements. This is accomplished by a function-space diffusion model and plug-and-play guidance for conditioning. Our method first trains an unconditional, discretization-agnostic denoising model using neural operator architectures. At inference, we refine the samples to satisfy sparse observation data via a gradient-based guidance mechanism. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, we extend Tweedie's formula to infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, providing the theoretical foundation for our posterior sampling approach. Our method (FunDPS) accurately captures posterior distributions in function spaces under minimal supervision and severe data scarcity. Across five PDE tasks with only 3% observation, our method achieves an average 32% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art fixed-resolution diffusion baselines while reducing sampling steps by 4x. Furthermore, multi-resolution fine-tuning ensures strong cross-resolution generalizability. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first diffusion-based framework to operate independently of discretization, offering a practical and flexible solution for forward and inverse problems in the context of PDEs. Code is available at https://github.com/neuraloperator/FunDPS

AI.title_translation: 函数空间上的引导扩散采样及其在偏微分方程中的应用
AI.tldr: 研究人员开发了一种名为FunDPS的、在函数空间上运行的扩散模型，用于从极少量的测量数据中求解复杂的偏微分方程（PDE）逆问题。它不需要预先确定离散网格，并且在性能和效率上都大幅优于现有技术。
AI.motivation: 针对PDE相关的逆问题，目标是从极度稀疏或有噪声的测量中恢复出完整的解。现有的方法可能受限于固定分辨率或数据稀疏性。
AI.method: 提出一个函数空间扩散模型框架，并结合即插即用的梯度指导机制进行条件采样。该方法首先使用神经算子架构训练一个无条件、不依赖离散化的去噪模型，然后在推理时通过基于梯度的指导机制来细化样本以满足稀疏观测数据。理论上，将Tweedie公式扩展到无限维Banach空间。
AI.result: 在五个具有仅3%观测数据的PDE任务中，FunDPS方法的准确率比最先进的固定分辨率扩散基线平均提高了32%，同时将采样步骤减少了4倍。该方法还通过多分辨率微调确保了强大的跨分辨率泛化能力。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的FunDPS方法能够在极度稀疏的观测数据下，准确地捕获函数空间中的后验分布，并在多个PDE任务中显著优于现有基线方法，同时提高了采样效率。该方法首次实现了独立于离散化的基于扩散的框架来解决前向和逆问题。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一个通用的条件采样框架，用于基于PDE的逆问题，目标是从极其稀疏或有噪声的测量中恢复整个解。这是通过一个函数空间扩散模型和用于条件化的即插即用引导来实现的。我们的方法首先使用神经算子架构训练一个无条件、不依赖离散化的去噪模型。在推理时，我们通过基于梯度的引导机制来完善样本，以满足稀疏的观测数据。通过严格的数学分析，我们将Tweedie公式扩展到无限维Banach空间，为我们的后验采样方法提供了理论基础。我们的方法（FunDPS）在最小监督和严重数据稀缺的情况下，能够准确地捕获函数空间中的后验分布。在五个仅有3%观测数据的PDE任务中，我们的方法与最先进的固定分辨率扩散基线相比，平均准确率提高了32%，同时采样步骤减少了4倍。此外，多分辨率微调确保了强大的跨分辨率泛化能力。据我们所知，这是第一个独立于离散化的基于扩散的框架，为PDE背景下的前向和逆问题提供了一个实用且灵活的解决方案。代码可在https://github.com/neuraloperator/FunDPS获取。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一个基于函数空间扩散模型和即插即用指导的通用框架（FunDPS），用于解决偏微分方程（PDE）相关的逆问题，目标是从极度稀疏的观测中恢复完整解。该方法利用神经算子和梯度指导，并在理论上将Tweedie公式推广到无限维空间，实现了不依赖离散化的采样，并在多项测试中显著超越了现有方法。
AI.keywords: 函数空间扩散模型, 偏微分方程, 逆问题, 引导采样, 神经算子
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于提出了一个在函数空间上操作的扩散模型框架，并结合了即插即用（plug-and-play）的指导机制来解决偏微分方程（PDE）的逆问题。其理论贡献是将Tweedie公式推广到无限维Banach空间。方法的关键优势在于其不依赖于离散化，这在处理PDE问题时提供了极大的灵活性和实用性。然而，摘要中未明确指出其局限性。

title: Robust Answers, Fragile Logic: Probing the Decoupling Hypothesis in LLM Reasoning
summary: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has become a cornerstone for complex reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs), the faithfulness of the generated reasoning remains an open question. We investigate the Decoupling Hypothesis: that correct answers often mask fragile, post-hoc rationalizations that are not causally tied to the model's prediction. To systematically verify this, we introduce MATCHA, a novel Answer-Conditioned Probing framework. Unlike standard evaluations that focus on final output accuracy, MATCHA isolates the reasoning phase by conditioning generation on the model's predicted answer, allowing us to stress-test the stability of the rationale itself. Our experiments reveal a critical vulnerability: under imperceptible input perturbations, LLMs frequently maintain the correct answer while generating inconsistent or nonsensical reasoning - effectively being ``Right for the Wrong Reasons''. Using LLM judges to quantify this robustness gap, we find that multi-step and commonsense tasks are significantly more susceptible to this decoupling than logical tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that adversarial examples generated by MATCHA transfer non-trivially to black-box models. Our findings expose the illusion of CoT robustness and underscore the need for future architectures that enforce genuine answer-reasoning consistency rather than mere surface-level accuracy.

AI.title_translation: 稳健的答案，脆弱的逻辑：探究大型语言模型推理中的去耦假设
AI.tldr: LLM的思维链推理（CoT）常常是“为错误的原因而得出正确答案”：即使输入只有微小变化，模型也能保持答案正确，但其推理过程变得荒谬。新工具MATCHA揭示了这种脆弱性，表明我们不能完全相信CoT的解释，尤其是在复杂任务中。
AI.motivation: 研究旨在探究思维链（CoT）提示生成的推理过程的忠实度，特别是验证“解耦假设”——即正确答案是否常常掩盖了与模型预测没有因果关系的、脆弱的事后合理化。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为MATCHA（Answer-Conditioned Probing framework）的新颖框架，该框架通过以模型预测的答案为条件来隔离推理阶段，从而对推理的稳定性进行压力测试。
AI.result: 实验表明，在几乎察觉不到的输入扰动下，LLM经常保持正确的答案但生成不一致或无意义的推理（即“为错误的原因而正确”）。使用LLM判官量化发现，多步和常识性任务比逻辑任务更容易出现这种去耦现象。此外，MATCHA生成的对抗样本可以非平凡地迁移到黑盒模型。
AI.conclusion: 研究结果揭示了思维链（CoT）鲁棒性的假象，并强调了未来架构需要强制执行真正的答案-推理一致性，而非仅仅关注表面准确性。
AI.translation: 尽管思维链（CoT）提示已成为大型语言模型（LLMs）复杂推理的基石，但生成推理的忠实度仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。我们研究了解耦假设：正确的答案常常掩盖了脆弱的、事后编造的、与模型的预测没有因果关系的合理化。为了系统地验证这一点，我们引入了MATCHA，一个新颖的答案条件探针框架。与关注最终输出准确性的标准评估不同，MATCHA通过以模型的预测答案为条件来隔离推理阶段，从而允许我们对推理本身的稳定性进行压力测试。我们的实验揭示了一个关键的漏洞：在几乎察觉不到的输入扰动下，LLM经常保持正确的答案，同时生成不一致或无意义的推理——有效地“为错误的原因而正确”。使用LLM判官量化这种鲁棒性差距，我们发现多步和常识性任务比逻辑任务更容易受到这种解耦的影响。此外，我们证明了由MATCHA生成的对抗样本可以非平凡地迁移到黑盒模型。我们的发现暴露了CoT鲁棒性的假象，并强调了未来需要强制执行真正答案-推理一致性而非仅仅表面准确性的架构。
AI.summary: 本文调查了大型语言模型（LLM）推理中的“解耦假设”，即正确答案可能与脆弱的推理过程分离。研究人员提出了MATCHA框架来隔离推理阶段并测试其稳定性。实验发现，LLM容易在微小输入扰动下保持正确答案但产生不一致的推理，表明思维链的鲁棒性存在错觉，尤其在多步和常识任务中更为明显。
AI.keywords: 思维链, 解耦假设, LLM推理, 鲁棒性, MATCHA
AI.comments: 这项工作创新性地提出了MATCHA框架来检验大型语言模型（LLM）推理中的“去耦假设”，即正确答案可能掩盖了脆弱的、事后编造的推理过程。实验结果揭示了CoT推理在面对微小输入扰动时缺乏鲁棒性，尤其在多步和常识性任务中表现明显，这指出了当前LLM“为错误的原因而得出正确答案”的普遍问题，对未来模型设计具有重要指导意义。

title: Position: The Real Barrier to LLM Agent Usability is Agentic ROI
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents represent a promising shift in human-AI interaction, moving beyond passive prompt-response systems to autonomous agents capable of reasoning, planning, and goal-directed action. While LLM agents are technically capable of performing a broad range of tasks, not all of these capabilities translate into meaningful usability. This position paper argues that the central question for LLM agent usability is no longer whether a task can be automated, but whether it delivers sufficient Agentic Return on Investment (Agentic ROI). Agentic ROI reframes evaluation from raw performance to a holistic, utility-driven perspective, guiding when, where, and for whom LLM agents should be deployed. Despite widespread application in high-ROI tasks like coding and scientific research, we identify a critical usability gap in mass-market, everyday applications. To address this, we propose a zigzag developmental trajectory: first scaling up to improve information gain and time savings, then scaling down to reduce cost. We present a strategic roadmap across these phases to make LLM agents truly usable, accessible, and scalable in real-world applications.

AI.title_translation: 职位：LLM代理可用性的真正障碍是代理投资回报率
AI.tldr: LLM代理的可用性瓶颈不是技术能力，而是投资回报率。文章提出了一个分阶段的开发策略，以提高LLM代理在日常应用中的可用性、可及性和可扩展性。
AI.motivation: LLM代理虽然技术上能力广泛，但并非所有能力都能转化为有意义的可用性。关键在于能否提供足够的代理投资回报率（Agentic ROI），而不仅仅是任务自动化能力。
AI.method: 提出Agentic ROI概念，从原始性能转向以效用为中心的整体评估方法。建议采用“之字形”发展轨迹：先扩大规模以提高信息获取和时间节省，再缩小规模以降低成本。
AI.result: LLM代理在编码和科学研究等高ROI任务中得到广泛应用，但在大众市场日常应用中存在关键的可用性差距。提出的策略旨在弥合这一差距。
AI.conclusion: LLM代理的真正可用性障碍是Agentic ROI。通过以效用为中心的方法和分阶段的开发策略，可以实现LLM代理在现实世界应用中的广泛可用性、可及性和可扩展性。
AI.translation: 大型语言模型（LLM）代理代表了人机交互的一个有希望的转变，从被动的提示-响应系统转向能够进行推理、规划和目标导向行动的自主代理。虽然LLM代理在技术上能够执行广泛的任务，但并非所有这些能力都能转化为有意义的可用性。这篇立场文章认为，LLM代理可用性的核心问题不再是任务是否可以自动化，而是它是否能提供足够的代理投资回报率（Agentic ROI）。Agentic ROI将评估从原始性能重新定义为以效用为中心的整体视角，指导何时、何地以及为谁部署LLM代理。尽管在编码和科学研究等高ROI任务中得到了广泛应用，但我们发现大众市场日常应用中存在关键的可用性差距。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了一条之字形的发展轨迹：首先扩大规模以提高信息获取和时间节省，然后缩小规模以降低成本。我们在这些阶段提出了一个战略路线图，以使LLM代理在现实世界的应用中真正可用、可及和可扩展。
AI.summary: 该论文认为，大型语言模型（LLM）代理可用性的关键在于其“代理投资回报率”（Agentic ROI），而非单纯的技术自动化能力。文章提出了一种以效用为中心的评估框架，并建议采用“之字形”发展策略——先通过扩大规模提升信息获取和时间节省效益，再通过缩小规模降低成本——以克服LLM代理在大众市场日常应用中的可用性差距，最终实现其广泛应用、可及性和可扩展性。
AI.keywords: LLM代理,可用性,代理投资回报率,之字形发展,可扩展性
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一个非常有见地且及时的观点，即LLM代理的成功部署应以“代理投资回报率”（Agentic ROI）为核心考量，而非仅仅关注技术上的可行性。这种以效用为中心的视角对于指导LLM代理的实际应用和商业化至关重要。提出的“之字形”发展轨迹也为实现LLM代理的可扩展性和可及性提供了一个清晰的战略框架。然而，文中并未详细阐述如何量化Agentic ROI的具体指标，这可能是未来研究的一个方向。此外，该论文作为一篇立场文章，更多地是提出了一个框架和观点，而非具体的实验验证。

title: LookWhere? Efficient Visual Recognition by Learning Where to Look and What to See from Self-Supervision
summary: Vision transformers are ever larger, more accurate, and more expensive to compute. The expense is even more extreme at high resolution as the number of tokens grows quadratically with the image size. We turn to adaptive computation to cope with this cost by learning to predict where to compute. Our LookWhere method divides the computation between a low-resolution selector and a high-resolution extractor without ever processing the full high-resolution input. We jointly pretrain the selector and extractor without task supervision by distillation from a self-supervised teacher, in effect, learning where and what to compute simultaneously. Unlike prior token reduction methods, which pay to save by pruning already-computed tokens, and prior token selection methods, which require complex and expensive per-task optimization, LookWhere economically and accurately selects and extracts transferrable representations of images. We show that LookWhere excels at sparse recognition on high-resolution inputs (Traffic Signs), maintaining accuracy while reducing FLOPs by up to 34x and time by 6x. It also excels at standard recognition tasks that are global (ImageNet classification) or local (ADE20K segmentation), improving accuracy while reducing time by 1.36x. See https://github.com/antofuller/lookwhere for the code and weights.

title: Differential Privacy Analysis of Decentralized Gossip Averaging under Varying Threat Models
summary: Achieving differential privacy (DP) guarantees in fully decentralized machine learning is challenging due to the absence of a central aggregator and varying trust assumptions among nodes. We present a framework for DP analysis of decentralized gossip-based averaging algorithms with additive node-level noise, from arbitrary views of nodes in a graph. We present an analytical framework based on a linear systems formulation that accurately characterizes privacy leakage between nodes. Our main contribution is showing that the DP guarantees are those of a Gaussian mechanism, where the growth of the squared sensitivity is asymptotically $O(T)$, where $T$ is the number of training rounds, similarly as in the case of central aggregation. As an application of the sensitivity analysis, we show that the excess risk of decentralized private learning for strongly convex losses is asymptotically similar as in centralized private learning.

title: SelfReflect: Can LLMs Communicate Their Internal Answer Distribution?
summary: The common approach to communicate a large language model's (LLM) uncertainty is to add a percentage number or a hedging word to its response. But is this all we can do? Instead of generating a single answer and then hedging it, an LLM that is fully transparent to the user needs to be able to reflect on its internal belief distribution and output a summary of all options it deems possible, and how likely they are. To test whether LLMs possess this capability, we develop the SelfReflect metric, an information-theoretic distance between a given summary and a distribution over answers. In interventional and human studies, we find that SelfReflect indicates even slight deviations, yielding a fine measure of faithfulness between a summary string and an LLM's actual internal distribution over answers. With SelfReflect, we make a resounding negative observation: modern LLMs are, across the board, incapable of revealing what they are uncertain about, neither through reasoning, nor chains-of-thoughts, nor explicit finetuning. However, we do find that LLMs are able to generate faithful summaries of their uncertainties if we help them by sampling multiple outputs and feeding them back into the context. This simple approach shines a light at the universal way of communicating LLM uncertainties whose future development the SelfReflect score enables. To support the development of this universal form of LLM uncertainties, we publish the code that implements our metric for arbitrary LLMs under https://github.com/apple/ml-selfreflect .

title: POLAR: A Benchmark for Multilingual, Multicultural, and Multi-Event Online Polarization
summary: Online polarization poses a growing challenge for democratic discourse, yet most computational social science research remains monolingual, culturally narrow, or event-specific. We introduce POLAR, a multilingual, multicultural, and multi-event dataset with over 110K instances in 22 languages drawn from diverse online platforms and real-world events. Polarization is annotated along three axes, namely detection, type, and manifestation, using a variety of annotation platforms adapted to each cultural context. We conduct two main experiments: (1) fine-tuning six pretrained small language models; and (2) evaluating a range of open and closed large language models in few-shot and zero-shot settings. The results show that, while most models perform well in binary polarization detection, they achieve substantially lower performance when predicting polarization types and manifestations. These findings highlight the complex, highly contextual nature of polarization and demonstrate the need for robust, adaptable approaches in NLP and computational social science. All resources will be released to support further research and effective mitigation of digital polarization globally.

title: Rethinking Multi-Modal Learning from Gradient Uncertainty
summary: Multi-Modal Learning (MML) integrates information from diverse modalities to improve predictive accuracy. While existing optimization strategies have made significant strides by mitigating gradient direction conflicts, we revisit MML from a gradient-based perspective to explore further improvements. Empirically, we observe an interesting phenomenon: performance fluctuations can persist in both conflict and non-conflict settings. Based on this, we argue that: beyond gradient direction, the intrinsic reliability of gradients acts as a decisive factor in optimization, necessitating the explicit modeling of gradient uncertainty. Guided by this insight, we propose Bayesian-Oriented Gradient Calibration for MML (BOGC-MML). Our approach explicitly models gradients as probability distributions to capture uncertainty, interpreting their precision as evidence within the framework of subjective logic and evidence theory. By subsequently aggregating these signals using a reduced Dempster's combination rule, BOGC-MML adaptively weights gradients based on their reliability to generate a calibrated update. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method.

title: Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin methods for scattering by periodic structures
summary: We propose a Trefftz discontinuous Galerkin (TDG) method for the approximation of plane wave scattering by periodic diffraction gratings, modelled by the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation. The periodic obstacle may include penetrable and impenetrable regions. The TDG method requires the approximation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operator on the periodic cell faces, and relies on plane wave discrete spaces. For polygonal meshes, all linear-system entries can be computed analytically. Using a Rellich identity, we prove a new explicit stability estimate for the Helmholtz solution, which is robust in the small material jump limit.

title: Are Your Generated Instances Truly Useful? GenBench-MILP: A Benchmark Suite for MILP Instance Generation
summary: The proliferation of machine learning-based methods for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) instance generation has surged, driven by the need for diverse training datasets. However, a critical question remains: Are these generated instances truly useful and realistic? Current evaluation protocols often rely on superficial structural metrics or simple solvability checks, which frequently fail to capture the true computational complexity of real-world problems. To bridge this gap, we introduce GenBench-MILP, a comprehensive benchmark suite designed for the standardized and objective evaluation of MILP generators. Our framework assesses instance quality across four key dimensions: mathematical validity, structural similarity, computational hardness, and utility in downstream tasks. A distinctive innovation of GenBench-MILP is the analysis of solver-internal features -- including root node gaps, heuristic success rates, and cut plane usage. By treating the solver's dynamic behavior as an expert assessment, we reveal nuanced computational discrepancies that static graph features miss. Our experiments on instance generative models demonstrate that instances with high structural similarity scores can still exhibit drastically divergent solver interactions and difficulty levels. By providing this multifaceted evaluation toolkit, GenBench-MILP aims to facilitate rigorous comparisons and guide the development of high-fidelity instance generators.

title: Many-for-Many: Unify the Training of Multiple Video and Image Generation and Manipulation Tasks
summary: Diffusion models have shown impressive performance in many visual generation and manipulation tasks. Many existing methods focus on training a model for a specific task, especially, text-to-video (T2V) generation, while many other works focus on finetuning the pretrained T2V model for image-to-video (I2V), video-to-video (V2V), image and video manipulation tasks, etc. However, training a strong T2V foundation model requires a large amount of high-quality annotations, which is very costly. In addition, many existing models can perform only one or several tasks. In this work, we introduce a unified framework, namely many-for-many, which leverages the available training data from many different visual generation and manipulation tasks to train a single model for those different tasks. Specifically, we design a lightweight adapter to unify the different conditions in different tasks, then employ a joint image-video learning strategy to progressively train the model from scratch. Our joint learning leads to a unified visual generation and manipulation model with improved video generation performance. In addition, we introduce depth maps as a condition to help our model better perceive the 3D space in visual generation. Two versions of our model are trained with different model sizes (8B and 2B), each of which can perform more than 10 different tasks. In particular, our 8B model demonstrates highly competitive performance in video generation tasks compared to open-source and even commercial engines. Our models and source codes are available at https://github.com/leeruibin/MfM.git.

title: The equivalent condition for GRL codes to be MDS, AMDS or self-dual
summary: It's well known that MDS, AMDS or self dual codes have good algebraic properties, and are applied in communication systems, data storage, quantum codes, and so on. In this paper, we focus on a class of generalized Roth-Lempel linear codes which are not not equivalent to linear codes in [21],[22] and give an equivalent condition for them or their dual to be non RS MDS, AMDS or non RS self-dual and some corresponding examples.

title: Interpretability by Design for Efficient Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
summary: Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) aims at optimising several, often conflicting goals to improve the flexibility and reliability of RL in practical tasks. This is typically achieved by finding a set of diverse, non-dominated policies that form a Pareto front in the performance space. We introduce LLE-MORL, an approach that achieves interpretability by design by utilising a training scheme based on the local relationship between the parameter space and the performance space. By exploiting a locally linear map between these spaces, our method provides an interpretation of policy parameters in terms of the objectives, and this structured representation enables an efficient search within contiguous solution domains, allowing for the rapid generation of high-quality solutions without extensive retraining. Experiments across diverse continuous control domains demonstrate that LLE-MORL consistently achieves higher Pareto front quality and efficiency than state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Statistically Valid Post-Deployment Monitoring Should Be Standard for AI-Based Digital Health
summary: This position paper argues that post-deployment monitoring in clinical AI is underdeveloped and proposes statistically valid and label-efficient testing frameworks as a principled foundation for ensuring reliability and safety in real-world deployment. A recent review found that only 9% of FDA-registered AI-based healthcare tools include a post-deployment surveillance plan. Existing monitoring approaches are often manual, sporadic, and reactive, making them ill-suited for the dynamic environments in which clinical models operate. We contend that post-deployment monitoring should be grounded in label-efficient and statistically valid testing frameworks, offering a principled alternative to current practices. We use the term "statistically valid" to refer to methods that provide explicit guarantees on error rates (e.g., Type I/II error), enable formal inference under pre-defined assumptions, and support reproducibility--features that align with regulatory requirements. Specifically, we propose that the detection of changes in the data and model performance degradation should be framed as distinct statistical hypothesis testing problems. Grounding monitoring in statistical rigor ensures a reproducible and scientifically sound basis for maintaining the reliability of clinical AI systems. Importantly, it also opens new research directions for the technical community--spanning theory, methods, and tools for statistically principled detection, attribution, and mitigation of post-deployment model failures in real-world settings.

title: Modern Minimal Perfect Hashing: A Survey
comments: Version 3 includes brief measurements of cache faults
summary:
Given a set $S$ of $n$ keys, a perfect hash function for $S$ maps the keys in $S$ to the first $m \geq n$ integers without collisions. It may return an arbitrary result for any key not in $S$ and is called minimal if $m = n$. The most important parameters are its space consumption, construction time, and query time. Years of research now enable modern perfect hash functions to be extremely fast to query, very space-efficient, and scale to billions of keys. Different approaches give different trade-offs between these aspects. For example, the smallest constructions get within 0.1% of the space lower bound of $\log_2(e)$ bits per key. Others are particularly fast to query, requiring only one memory access. Perfect hashing has many applications, for example to avoid collision resolution in static hash tables, and is used in databases, bioinformatics, and stringology.
  Since the last comprehensive survey in 1997, significant progress has been made. This survey covers the latest developments and provides a starting point for getting familiar with the topic. Additionally, our extensive experimental evaluation can serve as a guide to select a perfect hash function for use in applications.
comment: Version 3 includes brief measurements of cache faults

title: The pollution effect for FEM approximations of the Ginzburg-Landau equation
summary: In this paper, we investigate the approximation properties of solutions to the Ginzburg-Landau equation (GLE) in finite element spaces. Special attention is given to how the errors are influenced by coupling the mesh size $h$ and the polynomial degree $p$ of the finite element space to the size of the so-called Ginzburg-Landau material parameter $κ$. As observed in previous works, the finite element approximations to the GLE are suffering from a numerical pollution effect, that is, the best-approximation error in the finite element space converges under mild coupling conditions between $h$ and $κ$, whereas the actual finite element solutions possess poor accuracy in a large pre-asymptotic regime which depends on $κ$. In this paper, we provide a new error analysis that allows us to quantify the pre-asymptotic regime and the corresponding pollution effect in terms of explicit resolution conditions. In particular, we are able to prove that higher polynomial degrees reduce the pollution effect, i.e., the accuracy of the best-approximation is achieved under relaxed conditions for the mesh size. We provide both error estimates in the $H^1$- and the $L^2$-norm and we illustrate our findings with numerical examples.

title: GIQ: Benchmarking 3D Geometric Reasoning of Vision Foundation Models with Simulated and Real Polyhedra
comments: Accepted to ICLR 2026. Camera ready version
summary: Modern monocular 3D reconstruction methods and vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate impressive results on standard benchmarks, yet recent works cast doubt on their true understanding of geometric properties. We introduce GOQ, a comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the geometric reasoning capabilities of vision and vision-language foundation models. GIQ comprises synthetic and real-world images and corresponding 3D meshes of diverse polyhedra covering varying levels of complexity and symmetry, from Platonic, Archimedean, Johnson, and Catalan solids to stellations and compound shapes. Through systematic experiments involving monocular 3D reconstruction, 3D symmetry detection, mental rotation tests, and zero-shot shape classification tasks, we reveal significant shortcomings in current models. State-of-the-art reconstruction algorithms trained on extensive 3D datasets struggle to reconstruct even basic geometric Platonic solids accurately. Next, although foundation models may be shown via linear and non-linear probing to capture specific 3D symmetry elements, they falter significantly in tasks requiring detailed geometric differentiation, such as mental rotation. Moreover, advanced vision-language assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claud exhibit remarkably low accuracy in interpreting basic shape properties such as face geometry, convexity, and compound structures of complex polyhedra. GIQ is publicly available at toomanymatts.github.io/giq-benchmark/, providing a structured platform to benchmark critical gaps in geometric intelligence and facilitate future progress in robust, geometry-aware representation learning.

title: Automatic differentiation for performing the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya procedure in Lax-Wendroff type discretizations
summary: Lax-Wendroff methods combined with discontinuous Galerkin/flux reconstruction spatial discretization provide a high-order, single-stage, quadrature-free method for solving hyperbolic conservation laws. In this work, we introduce automatic differentiation (AD) for performing the Cauchy-Kowalewski procedure used in the element-local time average flux computation step (the predictor step) of Lax-Wendroff methods. The application of AD is similar for methods of any order and does not need positivity corrections during the predictor step. This contrasts with the approximate Lax-Wendroff procedure, which requires different finite difference formulas for different orders of the method and positivity corrections in the predictor step for fluxes that can only be computed on admissible states. The method is Jacobian-free and problem-independent, allowing direct application to any physical flux function. Numerical experiments demonstrate the order and positivity preservation of the method. Additionally, performance comparisons indicate that the wall-clock time of automatic differentiation is always on par with the approximate Lax-Wendroff method.

title: "Faithful to What?" On the Limits of Fidelity-Based Explanations
comments: 6 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to ICLR (Workshop on Scientific Methods for Understanding Deep Learning). Code available at https://github.com/jacksoneshbaugh/lambda-linearity-score/tree/main
summary: In explainable AI, surrogate models are commonly evaluated by their fidelity to a neural network's predictions. Fidelity, however, measures alignment to a learned model rather than alignment to the data-generating signal underlying the task. This work introduces the linearity score $λ(f)$, a diagnostic that quantifies the extent to which a regression network's input--output behavior is linearly decodable. $λ(f)$ is defined as an $R^2$ measure of surrogate fit to the network. Across synthetic and real-world regression datasets, we find that surrogates can achieve high fidelity to a neural network while failing to recover the predictive gains that distinguish the network from simpler models. In several cases, high-fidelity surrogates underperform even linear baselines trained directly on the data. These results demonstrate that explaining a model's behavior is not equivalent to explaining the task-relevant structure of the data, highlighting a limitation of fidelity-based explanations when used to reason about predictive performance.

title: Generalizable Trajectory Prediction via Inverse Reinforcement Learning with Mamba-Graph Architecture
summary: Accurate driving behavior modeling is fundamental to safe and efficient trajectory prediction, yet remains challenging in complex traffic scenarios. This paper presents a novel Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) framework that captures human-like decision-making by inferring diverse reward functions, enabling robust cross-scenario adaptability. The learned reward function is utilized to maximize the likelihood of output by integrating Mamba blocks for efficient long-sequence dependency modeling with graph attention networks to encode spatial interactions among traffic agents. Comprehensive evaluations on urban intersections and roundabouts demonstrate that the proposed method not only outperforms various popular approaches in terms of prediction accuracy but also achieves 2.3 times higher generalization performance to unseen scenarios compared to other baselines, achieving adaptability in Out-of-Distribution settings that is competitive with fine-tuning.

title: Verifying the Verifiers: Unveiling Pitfalls and Potentials in Fact Verifiers
summary: Fact verification is essential for ensuring the reliability of LLM applications. In this study, we evaluate 12 pre-trained LLMs and one specialized fact-verifier, including frontier LLMs and open-weight reasoning LLMs, using a collection of examples from 14 fact-checking benchmarks. We share three findings intended to guide future development of more robust fact verifiers. First, we highlight the importance of addressing annotation errors and ambiguity in datasets, demonstrating that approximately 16\% of ambiguous or incorrectly labeled data substantially influences model rankings. Neglecting this issue may result in misleading conclusions during comparative evaluations, and we suggest using a systematic pipeline utilizing LLM-as-a-judge to help identify these issues at scale. Second, we discover that frontier LLMs with few-shot in-context examples, often overlooked in previous works, achieve top-tier performance. We therefore recommend that future studies include comparisons with these simple yet highly effective baselines. Lastly, despite their effectiveness, frontier LLMs incur substantial costs, motivating the development of small, fine-tuned fact verifiers. We show that these small models still have room for improvement, particularly on instances that require complex reasoning. Encouragingly, we demonstrate that augmenting training with synthetic multi-hop reasoning data significantly enhances their capabilities in such instances. We release our code, model, and dataset at https://github.com/just1nseo/verifying-the-verifiers.

title: LittleBit: Ultra Low-Bit Quantization via Latent Factorization
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2025. Banseok Lee and Dongkyu Kim contributed equally
summary: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) is frequently hindered by prohibitive memory and computational requirements. While quantization mitigates these bottlenecks, maintaining model fidelity in the sub-1-bit regime remains a persistent challenge. In this paper, we introduce LittleBit, a novel framework for extreme LLM compression. We target quantization rates as low as $0.1$ bits per weight (BPW), achieving a memory reduction of approximately $31\times$, which effectively compresses Llama2-13B to under $0.9$ GB. We represent weights via low-rank latent matrix factorization and subsequently binarize the resulting factors. To counteract the information loss inherent to such drastic precision reduction, we integrate a multi-scale compensation mechanism that learns importance parameters across row, column, and latent dimensions. Two primary contributions enable effective training: Dual Sign-Value-Independent Decomposition (Dual-SVID) for quantization-aware training (QAT) initialization, and Residual Compensation to minimize approximation errors. Extensive experiments confirm the superiority of LittleBit in the sub-1-bit domain; for instance, our method at $0.1$ BPW surpasses the performance of leading techniques operating at $0.7$ BPW on Llama2-7B. We establish a new size-performance trade-off -- unlocking a potential $11.6\times$ inference speedup relative to FP16 -- and render powerful LLMs practical for resource-constrained environments. Our code is available at https://github.com/SamsungLabs/LittleBit.

title: Dissecting the SWE-Bench Leaderboards: Profiling Submitters and Architectures of LLM- and Agent-Based Repair Systems
comments: Part of this work (RQ1) has been published at the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE-SEIP 2026), DOI: 10.1145/3786583.3786904. The published version is also available on arXiv at arXiv:2602.04449
summary: The rapid progress in Automated Program Repair (APR) has been driven by advances in AI, particularly large language models (LLMs) and agent-based systems. SWE-Bench is a recent benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based repair systems using real issues and pull requests mined from 12 popular open-source Python repositories. Its public leaderboards -- SWE-Bench Lite and SWE-Bench Verified -- have become central platforms for tracking progress and comparing solutions. However, because the submission process does not require detailed documentation, the architectural design and origin of many solutions remain unclear. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive study of all submissions to the SWE-Bench Lite (79 entries) and Verified (99 entries) leaderboards, analyzing 80 unique approaches across dimensions such as submitter type, product availability, LLM usage, and system architecture. Our findings reveal the dominance of proprietary LLMs (especially Claude 3.5), the presence of both agentic and non-agentic designs, and a contributor base spanning from individual developers to large tech companies.
